method: Direct source inspection of contact.html (+10 locale copies), sample-request.html, jft-conversion.js, all 3 calculators, shipment-tracker.html, regional pages, and 3 targeted external web searches for B2B RFQ/commodity-exporter benchmark patterns.

personas.name: Food manufacturer/industrial buyer
personas.served: well (COA detail lives on export-documentation.html, a reasonable IA choice)

personas.name: New/cautious importer
personas.served: was the persona most exposed to the RFQ friction fixed this phase

findings.title: RFQ form requires Port of Discharge and Target Shipment Month, which a first-time buyer often cannot supply yet
findings.evidence: contact.html required 10 fields to submit. External benchmark (chatsku.com RFQ best practices): 'name, email, product, and quantity... those four are required. Everything else is optional.' Port and shipment month are pre-quote unknowns for many genuine buyers; country/packing/product remain required because they are price-determining for a bulk commodity quote.
findings.fix: removed the required attribute and the visual * marker from Port of Discharge (all 11 language copies) and Target Shipment Month (English only - the field does not exist on locale copies), replaced with an '(optional)' hint

findings.title: Locale contact.html copies lack a shipment_month field entirely (pre-existing structural drift vs English)
findings.reason: a locale form-field-parity project (also missing quantity/incoterm handling in some copies per Phase 11's own finding) is a separate, larger localization-architecture undertaking outside this phase's narrow RFQ-friction scope

areas_audited_no_defect_found: international/RTL conversion risk (structure-only fix, no new translated text)

competitive_benchmark.pattern: RFQ forms should require only name/email/product/quantity
spice/commodity exporters display ISO/HACCP/FSSAI/Spices Board + COA/lab documentation
competitive_benchmark.source: web search on spice exporter trust certifications

competitive_benchmark.pattern: WhatsApp used alongside (not instead of) a contact form for agro B2B trade
competitive_benchmark.source: web search on agricultural exporter WhatsApp vs contact form

rejected_ideas.reason: packing materially changes FOB/CIF unit economics for a bulk commodity; JFT cannot return a meaningful quote without it
documented as P13-F2 but out of this phase's narrow scope
explicitly out of scope per the phase brief
existing honest '1 Day - Typical Review' language is already correct and was not touched

expected_impact: fewer abandoned RFQ attempts from qualified buyers who have a real product/quantity/destination need but no firm port or ship-month yet, with zero loss of information from buyers who do provide it
risk_assessment: very low - removes only an HTML required constraint and a visual marker; no field deleted, no submission-handler change, no translated copy touched
